lines.t: In nineteen thirteen, a roulette wheel in Monte Carlo landed on black twenty-six times in a row.
lines.title: 26 TIMES *IN A ROW*

lines.t: After about fifteen blacks, gamblers rushed to bet on red. Surely red was due.
lines.title: "RED IS *DUE!*"

lines.t: It wasn't. The ball has no memory. Every spin has the same odds. And people lost millions of francs that night.
lines.title: THE BALL HAS *NO MEMORY*

lines.t: It's called the gambler's fallacy. And it's not just casinos. People do it with stocks, crypto and even sports.
lines.title: THE GAMBLER'S *FALLACY*

lines.t: Past results don't change future odds. Follow for more money psychology.
lines.title: DON'T FALL *FOR IT*
